_comment: P1-139. Two halves that must land together: a direction invariant at the single choke point every stop move routes through, and a re-arm that retries the move it actually lost instead of resetting a flag that recomputes a different price. Landing only the first LATCHES THE TRAIL OFF, which is P0-67's original defect restored -- TestAtm_P1139_TheTrailStillAdvancesAfterARefusedTrailMove is green at baseline precisely so it goes red if you do that. Three of the five P1-139 tests are green at baseline and are regression guards; do not delete or weaken any of them.

tickets.title: A stop never moves against the position, and a refused trail move retries the trail
tickets.defect: RequestStopMove will ask the broker to move a stop the WRONG WAY and report it as an advance. Measured, red at baseline: a long MNQ from 20000.00 whose trail has carried the stop to 20010.00 has ONE trail move to 20013.00 refused by the provider; ReconcileStopFromBroker counts the refusal and re-arms with `if (bracket.BreakevenTriggered && bracket.StopModifyAttempts < MaxStopModifyAttempts) bracket.BreakevenTriggered = false;`, and the SAME sweep then falls into the breakeven branch, whose target is CalculateBreakevenStopPrice(entryPrice, ...) = 20000.50 -- computed from ENTRY, with no knowledge of the stop. ShouldTriggerBreakeven compares current price to ENTRY only, so it is true and stays true for the life of a winning trade. The result is a request to move the stop DOWN 9.5 points on a live position, and ATM_STOP_MOVE_REQUESTED prints 'requested stop 20010 -> 20000.5' as if it were progress. There is no monotonic comparison at any of the three call sites nor inside RequestStopMove itself. Root cause: BreakevenTriggered carries three meanings -- 'breakeven has been reached' (breakeven branch), 'the trail may run' (trailing branch), and since P0-67 'retry the outstanding move' (reconciler). Clearing it to retry a BREAKEVEN move is correct and is what P0-67 was for. Clearing it to retry a TRAIL move recomputes the target from the wrong origin.
tickets.spec: Land ALL THREE parts. PART ONE, the invariant: RequestStopMove must refuse any newStopPrice that is not strictly better than the price the broker holds, before it calls ModifyStopPrice. Better is HIGHER for a long and LOWER for a short -- read bracket.IsLong, never the sign of a quantity. Equal prices are refused too: a redundant Change() is an order the provider can revert (P0-61) with nothing to gain. The baseline is bracket.CurrentStopPrice, and a bracket that has never reconciled holds 0 -- treat a non-positive baseline as NO BASELINE and allow the move, otherwise every SHORT's first move (19999.50 against 0) reads as wrong-way and the feature dies on half of all trades. This matches a convention the file ALREADY has: ReconcileStopFromBroker's external-move branch is gated `&& bracket.CurrentStopPrice > 0` for exactly this reason. Do NOT change CurrentStopPrice's default to double.NaN to get a cleaner sentinel -- that field is serialised into the bridge's ATM status payload by GetBracketStatus as `currentStop`, and NaN is not valid JSON, so every consumer of that route would throw on parse. A refusal made on our own behalf is not a provider refusal: it must NOT increment StopModifyAttempts, must NOT call AnnounceStopMoveAbandonmentIfNeeded, must leave RequestedStopPrice as NaN, must return false, and must log event name ATM_STOP_MOVE_WRONG_WAY via RiskGuardAddOn.LogFromComponent naming BOTH the price held and the price refused. PART TWO, the re-arm: only clear BreakevenTriggered when the move that was refused WAS the breakeven move. Record which kind of move is outstanding at the point RequestStopMove sets RequestedStopPrice, on a new ActiveBracket member, and clear it wherever RequestedStopPrice is cleared. Do NOT decide this by inspecting the `reason` string -- a display string driving control flow is a defect in its own right. Pass the kind explicitly from each of the three call sites. PART THREE, and the fix is WRONG without it: when the broker already holds a stop at or beyond the computed breakeven price, breakeven HAS been reached -- record it by setting BreakevenTriggered true WITHOUT issuing any request, rather than asking and being refused. Two reasons. It keeps the trailing block, which is gated on that flag, from latching off for the life of the position; and it keeps ATM_STOP_MOVE_WRONG_WAY off the normal path, so that event stays an anomaly rather than a line printed every five seconds on every winning trade. This state is reachable without any provider refusal at all: something outside this monitor can move the stop up (the reconciler has an ATM_STOP_MOVED_EXTERNALLY branch for it), and P2-136 re-adopts brackets whose flags are unset. Everything else about the reconciler stays exactly as it is: the CONFIRMED branch is still the only place StopModifyAttempts resets and the only place StopMoveAbandonAnnounced clears (P2-135 pins that with four assertions), and a refused BREAKEVEN move must still re-arm and re-request the same 20000.50 it was refused.

regions.note: RequestedStopPrice's NaN sentinel lives here and is documented at length; the new member recording WHICH move is outstanding belongs beside it and must be cleared wherever RequestedStopPrice is. StopModifyAttempts and StopMoveAbandonAnnounced are also here -- their comments are pinned by P2-134/P2-135 assertions, do not reword them.

Note the ORDER of the existing early returns: the in-flight check must stay first (a second Change() reverts the order), and the budget check must keep spending on every provider-side failure including the not-found one -- P1-130's whole content. The new guard is our own refusal and sits outside that budget.

The trailing branch's own `stopMoved` comparison against CurrentStopPrice stays -- it is a different question (is there anything to ask for) from the invariant (is what we are asking for safe).
